questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He finally / recalled that / the thieves have leave / from the front door.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: ​**the thieves have leave**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is related to the verb tense.
 
• In this case, the present perfect tense "**have leave**" is incorrect.
 
• The **correct form should be in the past tense**, as the action of leaving occurred before the recalling in the past.
 
• The **correct phrase** should be "**the thieves had left**."
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *He finally recalled that the thieves had left from the front door.*
 
• In this corrected sentence, the past perfect tense "**had left**" is used to indicate that the thieves left before the main action of recalling took place.

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A) Benefits of reading have been underlined since ages together.

B) Once they understand the sensibleness behind reading, they would pass it on to others as well.

C) It brings knowledge and wisdom both to the readers.

D) By virtue of a practice at home, this can be suggested to the young ones.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **ACDB**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sentence A: **This sentence **introduces the overarching theme of the importance** of reading and its enduring significance over time.
 
• **Sentence C: **This sentence **elaborates on one of the benefits of reading**, emphasizing the acquisition of knowledge and wisdom.
 
• **Sentence D: **This sentence **suggests a practical approach to instilling the habit of reading**, particularly among the young generation, by making it a household practice.
 
• **Sentence B: **This sentence **concludes the paragraph** by highlighting the idea that once individuals comprehend the rationale for reading, they are likely to share this understanding with others.
 
• So, the order **ACDB **creates a coherent flow of ideas, starting with the historical significance of reading, moving on to its benefits, suggesting a practical implementation at home, and concluding with the idea of passing on the understanding to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The flames caught so __quick__ that I had no time to think.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Quickly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of the sentence, "**quickly**" should be used to modify the verb "**caught**."
 
• Adverbs, like "**quickly**," are used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs and provide more information about how the action is performed.
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *The flames caught so quickly that I had no time to think.*
 
• So, "**quickly**" is the correct choice as it serves as an adverb, appropriately modifying the verb "caught" to convey the speed at which the flames ignited.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Quickest**" is an adjective and does not fit syntactically in the sentence. Adjectives modify nouns.
 
• "**As quick as**" is a comparative phrase, it is used to compare the speed of two actions or objects.
 
• "**Quicker**" is an adjective and doesn't fit the sentence structure.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.**

We will go to Spain this summer, __will we__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **won’t we?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence is a tag question, which is used to confirm or seek agreement on a statement.
 
• In English, **the tag question typically includes an auxiliary verb opposite in polarity to the main clause**.
 
• In this case, **the main clause is positive** ("We will go to Spain this summer"), so the **tag question should have a negative auxiliary verb**.
 
• So, the correct option to improve the underlined part of the given sentence is "**won’t we?**"
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *We will go to Spain this summer, won’t we?*
 
• The negative tag question provides a balanced and grammatically correct structure, seeking confirmation or agreement with the positive statement in the main clause.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The chef prepares the food in the kitchen.

options.text: The food will be prepared by the chef in the kitchen.
The food prepares by the chef in the kitchen.
The food is preparing by the chef in the kitchen.
The food is prepared by the chef in the kitchen.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The food is prepared by the chef in the kitchen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **passive **voice, the **object of the active sentence becomes the subject**, the **verb is changed to its passive form**, and the **original subject is mentioned as the agent** is introduced by the preposition "**by**."
 
• The prepositional phrase remains in the same position.
 
• **Active Voice Structure**: Subject + Verb + Object + Prepositional Phrase__
 __
 
• **Example**: *The gardener plants beautiful flowers in the garden. (Active)*
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice Structure**: Object (from the active sentence) + Verb (in passive form) + Agent ('by') + Prepositional Phrase__
 
 
• **Example**: *Beautiful flowers are planted in the garden by the gardener. (Passive)*
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

P. the golden era when their language, culture and arts flourished

Q. in the minds of the Tamils

R. under the patronage of successive Pandian kings

S. The name 'Madurai' evokes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **SQPR**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **S (Subject)**: "*The name 'Madurai'"* is the **subject **of the sentence. It **introduces **what the sentence is about.
 
• **Q (Qualifier)**: "*evokes in the minds of the Tamils*" is a **qualifier **that **provides additional information** about how the name 'Madurai' is perceived by the Tamils.
 
• **P (Predicate)**: "*the golden era when their language, culture, and arts flourished*" serves as the **predicate**, **explaining what 'Madurai' evokes**. It completes the **main idea** of the sentence.
 
• **R (Qualifier)**: "*under the patronage of successive Pandian kings*" **adds more detail about the historical context** of the golden era mentioned in the **predicate**.
 
• So, when arranged in the correct order (**SQPR**), the sentence reads: "*The name 'Madurai' evokes in the minds of the Tamils the golden era when their language, culture, and arts flourished under the patronage of successive Pandian kings.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.
